To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the poleward edge expansion of the Hadley circulation (the Hadley cell, HC) is driven by a decrease of baroclinicity, and the decrease in baroclimicity is caused by a decrease of the meridonal gradient of sea surface temperature in the outer tropic and subtropical regions.

1) the poleward shift of ITCZ in the seasonal cycle is the dominant mechanism driving the poleward shift (expansion) of the Hadley circulation (the HC) and 2) this mechanism is driven by a decrease of the angular momentum of Hadley circulation.
the width of the Hadley circulation is sensitive to ocean heat transport and that this sensitivity is primarily driven by the effect of ocean heat transport on the intertropical convergent zone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how ocean heat transport impacts the Hadley circulation, a key component of the global atmospheric circulation.
how the width of the Hadley circulation responds to an idealized representation of poleward ocean heat fluxes in an aquaplanet model.
how ocean circulation and oceanic heat transport affect the atmospheric circulation, in particular how they affect the Hadley circulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HC expands in response to poleward OHT because the baroclinicity at the poleward edge is reduced by 1) a poleward shift of ITCZ, 2) a decrease in subtropical static stabilities and 3) an increase in SST gradients in the subtropics.
the HC width is limited by the poleward extent to which baroclinic processes can be sustained.

the poleward ocean heat flux is responsible for the widening of Hadley cell, which is a result of the decrease in the angular velocity of the Hadley circulation, the increase in static stability, and the decrease of the meridial SST gradient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the width of the Hadley cell is determined primarily by the baroclinicity of the subtropical edge and the poleward edge, and is modulated primarily by the position of the intertropcial convergence zone and the meridional SST gradient.
poleward ocean heat transfer causes an expansion of the Hadley circulation by reducing baroclinicity.
the HC is a baroclinically controlled circulation that expands when poleward OHT weakens baroclinicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a poleward shift of HC extent in response to OHT is a robust feature of our model, and that the HC response to OHT can be understood in terms of the response of baroclinicity and ITCZ position.
HC width is sensitive to changes in baroclinic structure, which is in turn sensitive to the meridional structure of the SST field.
a poleward shift of HC edge is not a necessary consequence of poleward OHT.
